entries.4255: προαιρέομαι PROAIRE/OMAI proairéomai pro-ahee-reh'-om-ahee from G4253 and G138; to choose for oneself before another thing (prefer), i.e. (by implication) to propose (intend):--purpose.
entries.4256: προαιτιάομαι PROAITIA/OMAI proaitiáomai pro-ahee-tee-ah'-om-ahee from G4253 and a derivative of G156; to accuse already, i.e. previously charge:--prove before.
entries.4257: προακούω PROAKOU/W proakoúō pro-ak-oo'-o from G4253 and G191; to hear already,i.e. anticipate:--hear before.
entries.4258: προαμαρτάνω PROAMARTA/NW proamartánō pro-am-ar-tan'-o from G4253 and G264; to sin previously (to conversion):--sin already, heretofore sin.
entries.4259: προαύλιον PROAU/LION proaúlion pro-ow'-lee-on neuter of a presumed compound of G4253 and G833; a forecourt, i.e. vestibule (alley-way):--porch.
entries.4260: προβαίνω PROBAI/NW probaínō prob-ah'-ee-no from G4253 and the base of G939; to walk forward, i.e. advance (literally, or in years):--+ be of a great age, go farther (on), be well stricken.
entries.4261: προβάλλω PROBA/LLW probállō prob-al'-lo from G4253 and G906; to throw forward, i.e. push to the front, germinate:--put forward, shoot forth.
entries.4262: προβατικός PROBATIKO/S probatikós prob-at-ik-os' from G4263; relating to sheep, i.e. (a gate) through which they were led into Jerusalem:--sheep (market).
entries.4263: πρόβατον PRO/BATON próbaton prob'-at-on probably neuter of a presumed derivative of G4260; something that walks forward (a quadruped), i.e. (specially), a sheep (literally or figuratively):--sheep(-fold).
entries.4264: προβιβάζω PROBIBA/ZW probibázō prob-ib-ad'-zo from G4253 and a reduplicated form of G971; to force forward, i.e. bring to the front, instigate:--draw, before instruct.
entries.4265: προβλέπω PROBLE/PW problépō prob-lep'-o from G4253 and G991; to look out beforehand, i.e. furnish in advance:--provide.
entries.4266: προγίνομαι PROGI/NOMAI progínomai prog-in'-om-ahee from G4253 and G1096; to be already, i.e. have previousy transpired:--be past.
entries.4267: προγινώσκω PROGINW/SKW proginṓskō prog-in-oce'-ko from G4253 and G1097; to know beforehand, i.e. foresee:--foreknow (ordain), know (before).
entries.4268: πρόγνωσις PRO/GNWSIS prógnōsis prog'-no-sis from G4267; forethought:--foreknowledge.
entries.4269: πρόγονος PRO/GONOS prógonos prog'-on-os from G4266; an ancestor, (grand-)parent:--forefather, parent.
entries.4270: προγράφω PROGRA/FW prográphō prog-raf'-o from G4253 and G1125; to write previously; figuratively, to announce, prescribe:--before ordain, evidently set forth, write (afore, aforetime).
entries.4271: πρόδηλος PRO/DHLOS pródēlos prod'-ay-los from G4253 and G1212; plain before all men, i.e. obvious:--evident, manifest (open) beforehand.
entries.4272: προδίδωμι PRODI/DWMI prodídōmi prod-id'-o-mee from G4253 and G1325; to give before the other party has given:--first give.
entries.4273: προδότης PRODO/THS prodótēs prod-ot'-ace from G4272 (in the sense of giving forward into another's (the enemy's) hands); a surrender:--betrayer, traitor.
entries.4274: πρόδρομος PRO/DROMOS pródromos prod'-rom-os from the alternate of G4390; a runner ahead, i.e. scout (figuratively, precursor):--forerunner.
entries.4275: προείδω PROEI/DW proeídō pro-i'-do from G4253 and G1492; foresee:--foresee, saw before.
entries.4276: προελπίζω PROELPI/ZW proelpízō pro-el-pid'-zo from G4253 and G1679; to hope in advance of other confirmation:--first trust.
entries.4277: προέπω PROE/PW proépō pro-ep'-o from G4253 and G2036; to say already, to predict:--forewarn, say (speak, tell) before. Compare G4280.
entries.4278: προενάρχομαι PROENA/RXOMAI proenárchomai pro-en-ar'-khom-ahee from G4253 and G1728; to commence already:--begin (before).
entries.4279: προεπαγγέλλομαι PROEPAGGE/LLOMAI proepangéllomai pro-ep-ang-ghel'-lom-ahee middle voice from G4253 and G1861; to promise of old:--promise before.
entries.4280: προερέω PROERE/W proeréō pro-er-eh'-o from G4253 and G2046; used as alternate of G4277; to say already, predict:--foretell, say (speak, tell) before.
entries.4281: προέρχομαι PROE/RXOMAI proérchomai pro-er'-khom-ahee from G4253 and G2064 (including its alternate); to go onward, precede (in place or time):--go before (farther, forward), outgo, pass on.
entries.4282: προετοιμάζω PROETOIMA/ZW proetoimázō pro-et-oy-mad'-zo from G4253 and G2090; to fit up in advance (literally or figuratively):--ordain before, prepare afore.
entries.4283: προευαγγελίζομαι PROEUAGGELI/ZOMAI proeuangelízomai pro-yoo-ang-ghel-id'-zom-ahee middle voice from G4253 and G2097; to announce glad news in advance:--preach before the gospel.
entries.4284: προέχομαι PROE/XOMAI proéchomai pro-ekh-om-ahee middle voice from G4253 and G2192; to hold oneself before others, i.e. (figuratively) to excel:--be better.
entries.4285: προηγέομαι PROHGE/OMAI proēgéomai pro-ay-geh'-om-ahee from G4253 and G2233; to lead the way for others, i.e. show deference:--prefer.
entries.4286: πρόθεσις PRO/QESIS próthesis proth'-es-is from G4388; a setting forth, i.e. (figuratively) proposal (intention); specially, the show-bread (in the Temple) as exposed before God:--purpose, shew(-bread).
entries.4287: προθέσμιος PROQE/SMIOS prothésmios proth-es'-mee-os from G4253 and a derivative of G5087; fixed beforehand, i.e. (feminine with G2250 implied) a designated day:--time appointed.
entries.4288: προθυμία PROQUMI/A prothymía proth-oo-mee'-ah from G4289; predisposition, i.e. alacrity:--forwardness of mind, readiness (of mind), ready (willing) mind.
entries.4289: πρόθυμος PRO/QUMOS próthymos proth'-oo-mos from G4253 and G2372; forward in spirit, i.e. predisposed; neuter (as noun) alacrity:--ready, willing.
entries.4290: προθύμως PROQU/MWS prothýmōs proth-oo'-moce adverb from G4289; with alacrity:--willingly.
entries.4291: προΐστημι PROI/+STHMI proḯstēmi pro-is'-tay-mee from G4253 and G2476; to stand before, i.e. (in rank) to preside, or (by implication) to practise:--maintain, be over, rule.
entries.4292: προκαλέομαι PROKALE/OMAI prokaléomai prok-al-eh'-om-ahee middle voice from G4253 and G2564; to call forth to oneself (challenge), i.e. (by implication) to irritate:--provoke.
entries.4293: προκαταγγέλλω PROKATAGGE/LLW prokatangéllō prok-at-ang-ghel'-lo from G4253 and G2605; to anounce beforehand, i.e. predict, promise:--foretell, have notice, (shew) before.
entries.4294: προκαταρτίζω PROKATARTI/ZW prokatartízō prok-at-ar-tid'-zo from G4253 and G2675; to prepare in advance:--make up beforehand.
entries.4295: πρόκειμαι PRO/KEIMAI prókeimai prok'-i-mahee from G4253 and G2749; to lie before the view, i.e. (figuratively) to be present (to the mind), to stand forth (as an example or reward):--be first, set before (forth).
entries.4296: προκηρύσσω PROKHRU/SSW prokērýssō prok-ay-rooce'-so from G4253 and G2784; to herald (i.e. proclaim) in advance:--before (first) preach.
entries.4297: προκοπή PROKOPH/ prokopḗ prok-op-ay' from G4298; progress, i.e. advancement (subjectively or objectively):--furtherance, profit.
entries.4298: προκόπτω PROKO/PTW prokóptō prok-op'-to from G4253 and G2875; to drive forward (as if by beating), i.e. (figuratively and intransitively) to advance (in amount, to grow; in time, to be well along):--increase, proceed, profit, be far spent, wax.
entries.4299: πρόκριμα PRO/KRIMA prókrima prok'-ree-mah from a compound of G4253 and G2919; a prejudgment (prejudice), i.e. prepossession:--prefer one before another.
entries.4300: προκυρόω PROKURO/W prokyróō prok-oo-ro'-o from G4253 and G2964; to ratify previously:--confirm before.
entries.4301: προλαμβάνω PROLAMBA/NW prolambánō prol-am-ban'-o from G4253 and G2983; to take in advance, i.e. (literally) eat before others have an opportunity; (figuratively) to anticipate, surprise:--come aforehand, overtake, take before.
entries.4302: προλέγω PROLE/GW prolégō prol-eg'-o from G4253 and G3004; to say beforehand, i.e. predict, forewarn:--foretell, tell before.
entries.4303: προμαρτύρομαι PROMARTU/ROMAI promartýromai prom-ar-too'-rom-ahee from G4253 and G3143; to be a witness in advance i.e. predict:--testify beforehand.
entries.4304: προμελετάω PROMELETA/W promeletáō prom-el-et-ah'-o from G4253 and G3191; to premeditate:--meditate before.
entries.4305: προμεριμνάω PROMERIMNA/W promerimnáō prom-er-im-nah'-o from G4253 and G3309; to care (anxiously) in advance:--take thought beforehand.
entries.4306: προνοέω PRONOE/W pronoéō pron-o-eh'-o from G4253 and G3539; to consider in advance, i.e. look out for beforehand (actively, by way of maintenance for others; middle voice by way of circumspection for oneself):--provide (for).
entries.4307: πρόνοια PRO/NOIA prónoia pron'-oy-ah from G4306; forethought, i.e. provident care or supply:--providence, provision.
entries.4308: προοράω PROORA/W prooráō pro-or-ah'-o from G4253 and G3708; to behold in advance, i.e. (actively) to notice (another) previously, or (middle voice) to keep in (one's own) view:--foresee, see before.
entries.4309: προορίζω PROORI/ZW proorízō pro-or-id'-zo from G4253 and G3724; to limit in advance, i.e. (figuratively) predetermine:--determine before, ordain, predestinate.
entries.4310: προπάσχω PROPA/SXW propáschō prop-as'-kho from G4253 and G3958; to undergo hardship previously:--suffer before.
entries.4311: προπέμπω PROPE/MPW propémpō prop-em'-po from G4253 and G3992; to send forward, i.e. escort or aid in travel:--accompany, bring (forward) on journey (way), conduct forth.
entries.4312: προπετής PROPETH/S propetḗs prop-et-ace' from a compound of G4253 and G4098; falling forward, i.e. headlong (figuratively, precipitate):--heady, rash(-ly).
entries.4313: προπορεύομαι PROPOREU/OMAI proporeúomai prop-or-yoo'-om-ahee from G4253 and G4198; to precede (as guide or herald):--go before.
entries.4314: πρός PRO/S prós pros a strengthened form of G4253; a preposition of direction; forward to, i.e. toward (with the genitive case, the side of, i.e. pertaining to; with the dative case, by the side of, i.e. near to; usually with the accusative case, the place, time, occasion, or respect, which is the destination of the relation, i.e. whither or for which it is predicated):--about, according to , against, among, at, because of, before, between, (where-)by, for, X at thy house, in, for intent, nigh unto, of, which pertain to, that, to (the end that), X together, to (you) -ward, unto, with(-in). In the compound case, it denotes essentially the same applications, namely, motion towards, accession to, or nearness at.
entries.4315: προσάββατον PROSA/BBATON prosábbaton pros-ab'-bat-on from G4253 and G4521; a fore-sabbath, i.e. the Sabbath-eve:--day before the sabbath. Compare G3904.
entries.4316: προσαγορεύω PROSAGOREU/W prosagoreúō pros-ag-or-yoo'-o from G4314 and a derivative of G58 (mean to harangue); to address, i.e. salute by name:--call.
entries.4317: προσάγω PROSA/GW proságō pros-ag'-o from G4314 and G71; to lead towards, i.e. (transitively) to conduct near (summon, present), or (intransitively) to approach:--bring, draw near.
entries.4318: προσαγωγή PROSAGWGH/ prosagōgḗ pros-ag-ogue-ay' from G4317 (compare G72); admission:--access.
entries.4319: προσαιτέω PROSAITE/W prosaitéō pros-ahee-teh'-o from G4314 and G154; to ask repeatedly (importune), i.e. solicit:--beg.
entries.4320: προσαναβαίνω PROSANABAI/NW prosanabaínō pros-an-ab-ah'-ee-no from G4314 and G305; to ascend farther, i.e. be promoted (take an upper (more honorable) seat):--go up.
entries.4321: προσαναλίσκω PROSANALI/SKW prosanalískō pros-an-al-is'-ko from G4314 and G355; to expend further:--spend.
entries.4322: προσαναπληρόω PROSANAPLHRO/W prosanaplēróō pros-an-ap-lay-ro'-o from G4314 and G378; to fill up further, i.e. furnish fully:--supply.
entries.4323: προσανατίθημι PROSANATI/QHMI prosanatíthēmi pros-an-at-ith'-ay-mee from G4314 and G394; to lay up in addition, i.e. (middle voice and figuratively) to impart or (by implication) to consult:--in conference add, confer.
entries.4324: προσαπειλέω PROSAPEILE/W prosapeiléō pros-ap-i-leh'-o from G4314 and G546; to menace additionally:--i.e. threaten further.
entries.4325: προσδαπανάω PROSDAPANA/W prosdapanáō pros-dap-an-ah'-o from G4314 and G1159; to expend additionally:--spend more.
entries.4326: προσδέομαι PROSDE/OMAI prosdéomai pros-deh'-om-ahee from G4314 and G1189; to require additionally, i.e. want further:--need.
entries.4327: προσδέχομαι PROSDE/XOMAI prosdéchomai pros-dekh'-om-ahee from G4314 and G1209; to admit (to intercourse, hospitality, credence, or (figuratively) endurance); by implication, to await (with confidence or patience):--accept, allow, look (wait) for, take.
entries.4328: προσδοκάω PROSDOKA/W prosdokáō pros-dok-ah'-o from G4314 and dokeuo (to watch); to anticipate (in thought, hope or fear); by implication, to await:--(be in) expect(-ation), look (for), when looked, tarry, wait for.
entries.4329: προσδοκία PROSDOKI/A prosdokía pros-dok-ee'-ah from G4328; apprehension (of evil); by implication, infliction anticipated:--expectation, looking after.
entries.4330: προσεάω PROSEA/W proseáō pros-eh-ah'-o from G4314 and G1439; to permit further progress:--suffer.
entries.4331: προσεγγίζω PROSEGGI/ZW prosengízō pros-eng-ghid'-zo from G4314 and G1448; to approach near:--come nigh.
entries.4332: προσεδρεύω PROSEDREU/W prosedreúō pros-ed-ryoo'-o from a compound of G4314 and the base of G1476; to sit near, i.e. attend as a servant:--wait at.
entries.4333: προσεργάζομαι PROSERGA/ZOMAI prosergázomai pros-er-gad'-zom-ahee from G4314 and G2038; to work additionally, i.e. (by implication) acquire besides:--gain.
entries.4334: προσέρχομαι PROSE/RXOMAI prosérchomai pros-er'-khom-ahee from G4314 and G2064 (including its alternate); to approach, i.e. (literally) come near, visit, or (figuratively) worship, assent to:--(as soon as he) come (unto), come thereunto, consent, draw near, go (near, to, unto).
entries.4335: προσευχή PROSEUXH/ proseuchḗ pros-yoo-khay' from G4336; prayer (worship); by implication, an oratory (chapel):--X pray earnestly, prayer.
entries.4336: προσεύχομαι PROSEU/XOMAI proseúchomai pros-yoo'-khom-ahee from G4314 and G2172; to pray to God, i.e. supplicate, worship:--pray (X earnestly, for), make prayer.
entries.4337: προσέχω PROSE/XW proséchō pros-ekh'-o from G4314 and G2192; (figuratively) to hold the mind (3563 implied) towards, i.e. pay attention to, be cautious about, apply oneself to, adhere to:--(give) attend(-ance, -ance at, -ance to, unto), beware, be given to, give (take) heed (to unto); have regard.
entries.4338: προσηλόω PROSHLO/W prosēlóō pros-ay-lo'-o from G4314 and a derivative of G2247; to peg to, i.e. spike fast:--nail to.
entries.4339: προσήλυτος PROSH/LUTOS prosḗlytos pros-ay'-loo-tos from the alternate of G4334; an arriver from a foreign region, i.e. (specially), an acceder (convert) to Judaism ("proselyte"):--proselyte.
entries.4340: πρόσκαιρος PRO/SKAIROS próskairos pros'-kahee-ros from G4314 and G2540; for the occasion only, i.e. temporary:--dur-(eth) for awhile, endure for a time, for a season, temporal.
entries.4341: προσκαλέομαι PROSKALE/OMAI proskaléomai pros-kal-eh'-om-ahee middle voice from G4314 and G2564; to call toward oneself, i.e. summon, invite:--call (for, to, unto).
entries.4342: προσκαρτερέω PROSKARTERE/W proskarteréō pros-kar-ter-eh'-o from G4314 and G2594; to be earnest towards, i.e. (to a thing) to persevere, be constantly diligent, or (in a place) to attend assiduously all the exercises, or (to a person) to adhere closely to (as a servitor):--attend (give self) continually (upon), continue (in, instant in, with), wait on (continually).
entries.4343: προσκαρτέρησις PROSKARTE/RHSIS proskartérēsis pros-kar-ter'-ay-sis from G4342; persistancy:--perseverance.
entries.4344: προσκεφάλαιον PROSKEFA/LAION proskephálaion pros-kef-al'-ahee-on neuter of a presumed compound of G4314 and G2776; something for the head, i.e. a cushion:--pillow.
entries.4345: προσκληρόω PROSKLHRO/W prosklēróō pros-klay-ro'-o from G4314 and G2820; to give a common lot to, i.e. (figuratively) to associate with:--consort with.
entries.4346: πρόσκλισις PRO/SKLISIS prósklisis pros'-klis-is from a compound of G4314 and G2827; a leaning towards, i.e. (figuratively) proclivity (favoritism):--partiality.
entries.4347: προσκολλάω PROSKOLLA/W proskolláō pros-kol-lah'-o from G4314 and G2853; to glue to, i.e. (figuratively) to adhere:--cleave, join (self).
entries.4348: πρόσκομμα PRO/SKOMMA próskomma pros'-kom-mah from G4350; a stub, i.e. (figuratively) occasion of apostasy:--offence, stumbling(-block, (-stone)).
entries.4349: προσκοπή PROSKOPH/ proskopḗ pros-kop-ay' from G4350; a stumbling, i.e. (figuratively and concretely) occasion of sin:--offence.
entries.4350: προσκόπτω PROSKO/PTW proskóptō pros-kop'-to from G4314 and G2875; to strike at, i.e. surge against (as water); specially, to stub on, i.e. trip up (literally or figuratively):--beat upon, dash, stumble (at).
entries.4351: προσκυλίω PROSKULI/W proskylíō pros-koo-lee'-o from G4314 and G2947; to roll towards, i.e. block against:--roll (to).
entries.4352: προσκυνέω PROSKUNE/W proskynéō pros-koo-neh'-o from G4314 and a probable derivative of G2965 (meaning to kiss, like a dog licking his master's hand); to fawn or crouch to, i.e. (literally or figuratively) prostrate oneself in homage (do reverence to, adore):--worship.
entries.4353: προσκυνητής PROSKUNHTH/S proskynētḗs pros-koo-nay-tace' from G4352; an adorer:--worshipper.
entries.4354: προσλαλέω PROSLALE/W proslaléō pros-lal-eh'-o from G4314 and G2980; to talk to, i.e. converse with:--speak to (with).
entries.4355: προσλαμβάνω PROSLAMBA/NW proslambánō pros-lam-ban'-o from G4314 and G2983; to take to oneself, i.e. use (food), lead (aside), admit (to friendship or hospitality):--receive, take (unto).
entries.4356: πρόσληψις PRO/SLHYIS próslēpsis pros'-lape-sis from G4355; admission:--receiving.
entries.4357: προσμένω PROSME/NW prosménō pros-men'-o from G4314 and G3306; to stay further, i.e. remain in a place, with a person; figuratively, to adhere to, persevere in:--abide still, be with, cleave unto, continue in (with).
entries.4358: προσορμίζω PROSORMI/ZW prosormízō pros-or-mid'-zo from G4314 and a derivative of the same as G3730 (meaning to tie (anchor) or lull); to moor to, i.e. (by implication) land at:--draw to the shore.
entries.4359: προσοφείλω PROSOFEI/LW prosopheílō pros-of-i'-lo from G4314 and G3784; to be indebted additionally:--over besides.
entries.4360: προσοχθίζω PROSOXQI/ZW prosochthízō pros-okh-thid'-zo from G4314 and a form of ὀχθέω O)XQE/W ochthéō (to be vexed with something irksome); to feel indignant at:--be grieved at.
entries.4361: πρόσπεινος PRO/SPEINOS próspeinos pros'-pi-nos from G4314 and the same as G3983; hungering further, i.e. intensely hungry:--very hungry.
entries.4362: προσπήγνυμι PROSPH/GNUMI prospḗgnymi pros-payg'-noo-mee from G4314 and G4078; to fasten to, i.e. (specially), to impale (on a cross):--crucify.
entries.4363: προσπίπτω PROSPI/PTW prospíptō pros-pip'-to from G4314 and G4098; to fall towards, i.e. (gently) prostrate oneself (in supplication or homage), or (violently) to rush upon (in storm):--beat upon, fall (down) at (before).
entries.4364: προσποιέομαι PROSPOIE/OMAI prospoiéomai pros-poy-eh'-om-ahee middle voice from G4314 and G4160; to do forward for oneself, i.e. pretend (as if about to do a thing):--make as though.
entries.4365: προσπορεύομαι PROSPOREU/OMAI prosporeúomai pros-por-yoo'-om-ahee from G4314 and G4198; to journey towards, i.e. approach (not the same as G4313):--go before.
entries.4366: προσρήγνυμι PROSRH/GNUMI prosrḗgnymi pros-rayg'-noo-mee from G4314 and G4486; to tear towards, i.e. burst upon (as a tempest or flood):--beat vehemently against (upon).
entries.4367: προστάσσω PROSTA/SSW prostássō pros-tas'-so from G4314 and G5021; to arrange towards, i.e. (figuratively) enjoin:--bid, command.
entries.4368: προστάτις PROSTA/TIS prostátis pros-tat'-is feminine of a derivative of G4291; a patroness, i.e. assistant:--succourer.
entries.4369: προστίθημι PROSTI/QHMI prostíthēmi pros-tith'-ay-mee from G4314 and G5087; to place additionally, i.e. lay beside, annex, repeat:--add, again, give more, increase, lay unto, proceed further, speak to any more.
entries.4370: προστρέχω PROSTRE/XW prostréchō pros-trekh'-o from G4314 and G5143 (including its alternate); to run towards, i.e. hasten to meet or join:--run (thither to, to).
entries.4371: προσφάγιον PROSFA/GION prosphágion pros-fag'-ee-on neuter of a presumed derivative of a compound of G4314 and G5315; something eaten in addition to bread, i.e. a relish (specially, fish; compare G3795):--meat.
entries.4372: πρόσφατος PRO/SFATOS prósphatos pros'-fat-os from G4253 and a derivative of G4969; previously (recently) slain (fresh), i.e. (figuratively) lately made:--new.
entries.4373: προσφάτως PROSFA/TWS prosphátōs pros-fat'-oce adverb from G4372; recently:--lately.
entries.4374: προσφέρω PROSFE/RW prosphérō pros-fer'-o from G4314 and G5342 (including its alternate); to bear towards, i.e. lead to, tender (especially to God), treat:--bring (to, unto), deal with, do, offer (unto, up), present unto, put to.
entries.4375: προσφιλής PROSFILH/S prosphilḗs pros-fee-lace' from a presumed compound of G4314 and G5368; friendly towards, i.e. acceptable:--lovely.
entries.4376: προσφορά PROSFORA/ prosphorá pros-for-ah' from G4374; presentation; concretely, an oblation (bloodless) or sacrifice:--offering (up).
entries.4377: προσφωνέω PROSFWNE/W prosphōnéō pros-fo-neh'-o from G4314 and G5455; to sound towards, i.e. address, exclaim, summon:--call unto, speak (un-)to.
entries.4378: πρόσχυσις PRO/SXUSIS próschysis pros'-khoo-sis from a compound of G4314 and χέω XE/W chéō (to pour); a shedding forth, i.e. affusion:--sprinkling.
entries.4379: προσψαύω PROSYAU/W prospsaúō pros-psow'-o from G4314 and ψαύω YAU/W psaúō (to touch); to impinge, i.e. lay a finger on (in order to relieve):--touch.
entries.4380: προσωποληπτέω PROSWPOLHPTE/W prosōpolēptéō pros-o-pol-ape-teh'-o from G4381; to favor an individual, i.e. show partiality:--have respect to persons.
entries.4381: προσωπολήπτης PROSWPOLH/PTHS prosōpolḗptēs pros-o-pol-ape'-tace from G4383 and G2983; an accepter of a face (individual), i.e. (specially), one exhibiting partiality:--respecter of persons.
entries.4382: προσωποληψία PROSWPOLHYI/A prosōpolēpsía pros-o-pol-ape-see'-ah from G4381; partiality, i.e. favoritism:--respect of persons.
entries.4383: πρόσωπον PRO/SWPON prósōpon pros'-o-pon from G4314 and ὤψ W)/Y ṓps (the visage, from G3700); the front (as being towards view), i.e. the countenance, aspect, appearance, surface; by implication, presence, person:--(outward) appearance, X before, countenance, face, fashion, (men's) person, presence.
entries.4384: προτάσσω PROTA/SSW protássō prot-as'-so from G4253 and G5021; to pre-arrange, i.e. prescribe:--before appoint.
entries.4385: προτείνω PROTEI/NW proteínō prot-i'-no from G4253 and τείνω TEI/NW teínō (to stretch); to protend, i.e. tie prostrate (for scourging):--bind.
entries.4386: πρότερον PRO/TERON próteron prot'-er-on neuter of G4387 as adverb (with or without the article); previously:--before, (at the) first, former.
entries.4387: πρότερος PRO/TEROS próteros prot'-er-os comparative of G4253; prior or previous:--former.
entries.4388: προτίθεμαι PROTI/QEMAI protíthemai prot-ith'-em-ahee middle voice from G4253 and G5087; to place before, i.e. (for oneself) to exhibit; (to oneself) to propose (determine):--purpose, set forth.
entries.4389: προτρέπομαι PROTRE/POMAI protrépomai prot-rep'-om-ahee middle voice from G4253 and the base of G5157; to turn forward for oneself, i.e. encourage:--exhort.
entries.4390: προτρέχω PROTRE/XW protréchō prot-rekh'-o from G4253 and G5143 (including its alternate); to run forward, i.e. outstrip, precede:--outrun, run before.
entries.4391: προϋπάρχω PROU+PA/RXW proÿpárchō pro-oop-ar'-kho from G4253 and G5225; to exist before, i.e. (adverbially) to be or do something previously:--+ be before(-time).
entries.4392: πρόφασις PRO/FASIS próphasis prof'-as-is from a compound of G4253 and G5316; an outward showing, i.e. pretext:--cloke, colour, pretence, show.
entries.4393: προφέρω PROFE/RW prophérō prof-er'-o from G4253 and G5342; to bear forward, i.e. produce:--bring forth.
entries.4394: προφητεία PROFHTEI/A prophēteía prof-ay-ti'-ah from G4396 ("prophecy"); prediction (scriptural or other):--prophecy, prophesying.
entries.4395: προφητεύω PROFHTEU/W prophēteúō prof-ate-yoo'-o from G4396; to foretell events, divine, speak under inspiration, exercise the prophetic office:--prophesy.
entries.4396: προφήτης PROFH/THS prophḗtēs prof-ay'-tace from a compound of G4253 and G5346; a foreteller ("prophet"); by analogy, an inspired speaker; by extension, a poet:--prophet.
entries.4397: προφητικός PROFHTIKO/S prophētikós prof-ay-tik-os' from G4396; pertaining to a foreteller ("prophetic"):--of prophecy, of the prophets.
entries.4398: προφῆτις PROFH=TIS prophētis prof-ay'-tis feminine of G4396; a female foreteller or an inspired woman:--prophetess.
entries.4399: προφθάνω PROFQA/NW prophthánō prof-than'-o from G4253 and G5348; to get an earlier start of, i.e. anticipate:--prevent.
entries.4400: προχειρίζομαι PROXEIRI/ZOMAI procheirízomai prokh-i-rid'-zom-ahee middle voice from G4253 and a derivative of G5495; to handle for oneself in advance, i.e. (figuratively) to purpose:--choose, make.
entries.4401: προχειροτονέω PROXEIROTONE/W procheirotonéō prokh-i-rot-on-eh'-o from G4253 and G5500; to elect in advance:--choose before.
entries.4402: Πρόχορος *PRO/XOROS Próchoros prokh'-or-os from G4253 and G5525; before the dance; Prochorus, a Christian:--Prochorus.
entries.4403: πρύμνα PRU/MNA prýmna proom'-nah feminine of πρυμνύς PRUMNU/S prymnýs (hindmost); the stern of a ship:--hinder part, stern.
entries.4404: πρωΐ PRWI/+ prōḯ pro-ee' adverb from G4253; at dawn; by implication, the day-break watch:--early (in the morning), (in the) morning.
entries.4405: πρωΐα PRWI/+A prōḯa pro-ee'-ah feminine of a derivative of G4404 as noun; day-dawn:--early, morning.
entries.4406: πρώϊμος PRW/I+MOS prṓïmos pro'-ee-mos from G4404; dawning, i.e. (by analogy) autumnal (showering, the first of the rainy season):--early.
entries.4407: πρωϊνός PRWI+NO/S prōïnós pro-ee-nos' from G4404; pertaining to the dawn, i.e. matutinal:--morning.
entries.4408: πρῶρα PRW=RA prōra pro'-ra feminine of a presumed derivative of G4253 as noun; the prow, i.e. forward part of a vessel:--forepart(-ship).
entries.4409: πρωτεύω PRWTEU/W prōteúō prote-yoo'-o from G4413; to be first (in rank or influence):--have the preeminence.
entries.4410: πρωτοκαθεδρία PRWTOKAQEDRI/A prōtokathedría pro-tok-ath-ed-ree'-ah from G4413 and G2515; a sitting first (in the front row), i.e. preeminence in council:--chief (highest, uppermost) seat.
entries.4411: πρωτοκλισία PRWTOKLISI/A prōtoklisía pro-tok-lis-ee'-ah from G4413 and G2828; a reclining first (in the place of honor) at the dinner-bed, i.e. preeminence at meals:--chief (highest, uppermost) room.
entries.4412: πρῶτον PRW=TON prōton pro'-ton neuter of G4413 as adverb (with or without G3588); firstly (in time, place, order, or importance):--before, at the beginning, chiefly (at, at the) first (of all).
entries.4413: πρῶτος PRW=TOS prōtos pro'-tos contracted superlative of G4253; foremost (in time, place, order or importance):--before, beginning, best, chief(-est), first (of all), former.
entries.4414: πρωτοστάτης PRWTOSTA/THS prōtostátēs pro-tos-tat'-ace from G4413 and G2476; one standing first in the ranks, i.e. a captain (champion):--ringleader.
entries.4415: πρωτοτόκια PRWTOTO/KIA prōtotókia pro-tot-ok'-ee-ah from G4416; primogeniture (as a privilege):--birthright.
entries.4416: πρωτότοκος PRWTO/TOKOS prōtótokos pro-tot-ok'-os from G4413 and the alternate of G5088; first-born (usually as noun, literally or figuratively):--firstbegotten(-born).
entries.4417: πταίω PTAI/W ptaíō ptah'-yo a form of G4098; to trip, i.e. (figuratively) to err, sin, fail (of salvation):--fall, offend, stumble.
entries.4418: πτέρνα PTE/RNA ptérna pter'-nah of uncertain derivation; the heel (figuratively):--heel.
entries.4419: πτερύγιον PTERU/GION pterýgion pter-oog'-ee-on neuter of a presumed derivative of G4420; a winglet, i.e. (figuratively) extremity (top corner):--pinnacle.
entries.4420: πτέρυξ PTE/RUC ptéryx pter'-oox from a derivative of G4072 (meaning a feather); a wing:--wing.
entries.4421: πτηνόν PTHNO/N ptēnón ptay-non' contraction for G4071; a bird:--bird.
entries.4422: πτοέω PTOE/W ptoéō pto-eh'-o probably akin to the alternate of G4098 (through the idea of causing to fall) or to G4072 (through that of causing to fly away); to scare:--frighten.
entries.4423: πτόησις PTO/HSIS ptóēsis pto'-ay-sis from G4422; alarm:--amazement.
entries.4424: Πτολεμαΐς *PTOLEMAI/+S Ptolemaḯs ptol-em-ah-is' from Πτολεμαῖος *PTOLEMAI=OS Ptolemaîos (Ptolemy, after whom it was named); Ptolemais, a place in Palestine:--Ptolemais.
entries.4425: πτύον PTU/ON ptýon ptoo'-on from G4429; a winnowing-fork (as scattering like spittle):--fan.
entries.4426: πτύρω PTU/RW ptýrō ptoo'-ro from a presumed derivative of G4429 (and thus akin to G4422); to frighten:--terrify.
entries.4427: πτύσμα PTU/SMA ptýsma ptoos'-mah from G4429; saliva:--spittle.
entries.4428: πτύσσω PTU/SSW ptýssō ptoos'-so probably akin to πετάννυμι PETA/NNUMI petánnymi (to spread; and thus apparently allied to G4072 through the idea of expansion, and to 4429 through that of flattening; compare G3961); to fold, i.e. furl a scroll:--close.
entries.4429: πτύω PTU/W ptýō ptoo'-o a primary verb (compare G4428); to spit:--spit.
entries.4430: πτῶμα PTW=MA ptōma pto'-mah from the alternate of G4098; a ruin, i.e. (specially), lifeless body (corpse, carrion):--dead body, carcase, corpse.
entries.4431: πτῶσις PTW=SIS ptōsis pto'-sis from the alternate of G4098; a crash, i.e. downfall (literally or figuratively):--fall.
entries.4432: πτωχεία PTWXEI/A ptōcheía pto-khi'-ah from G4433; beggary, i.e. indigence (literally or figuratively):--poverty.
entries.4433: πτωχεύω PTWXEU/W ptōcheúō pto-khyoo'-o from G4434; to be a beggar, i.e. (by implication) to become indigent (figuratively):--become poor.
entries.4434: πτωχός PTWXO/S ptōchós pto-khos' from πτώσσω PTW/SSW ptṓssō (to crouch); akin to G4422 and the alternate of G4098); a beggar (as cringing), i.e. pauper (strictly denoting absolute or public mendicancy, although also used in a qualified or relative sense; whereas G3993 properly means only straitened circumstances in private), literally (often as noun) or figuratively (distressed):--beggar(-ly), poor.
entries.4435: πυγμή PUGMH/ pygmḗ poog-may' from a primary πύξ PU/C pýx (the fist as a weapon); the clenched hand, i.e. (only in dative case as adverb) with the fist (hard scrubbing):--oft.
entries.4436: Πύθων *PU/QWN Pýthōn poo'-thone from Πυθώ *PUQW/ Pythṓ (the name of the region where Delphi, the seat of the famous oracle, was located); a Python, i.e. (by analogy, with the supposed diviner there) inspiration (soothsaying):-- divination.
entries.4437: πυκνός PUKNO/S pyknós pook-nos' from the same as G4635; clasped (thick), i.e. (figuratively) frequent; neuter plural (as adverb) frequently:--often(-er).
entries.4438: πυκτέω PUKTE/W pyktéō pook-teh'-o from a derivative of the same as G4435; to box (with the fist), i.e. contend (as a boxer) at the games (figuratively):--fight.
entries.4439: πύλη PU/LH pýlē poo'-lay apparently a primary word; a gate, i.e. the leaf or wing of a folding entrance (literally or figuratively):--gate.
entries.4440: πυλών PULW/N pylṓn poo-lone' from G4439; a gate-way, door-way of a building or city; by implication, a portal or vestibule:--gate, porch.
entries.4441: πυνθάνομαι PUNQA/NOMAI pynthánomai poon-than'-om-ahee middle voice prolonged from a primary πύθω PU/QW pýthō (which occurs only as an alternate in certain tenses); to question, i.e. ascertain by inquiry (as a matter of information merely; and thus differing from G2065, which properly means a request as a favor; and from G154, which is strictly a demand for something due; as well as from G2212, which implies a search for something hidden; and from G1189, which involves the idea of urgent need); by implication, to learn (by casual intelligence):--ask, demand, enquire, understand.
entries.4442: πῦρ PU=R pŷr poor a primary word; "fire" (literally or figuratively, specially, lightning):--fiery, fire.
entries.4443: πυρά PURA/ pyrá poo-rah' from G4442; a fire (concretely):--fire.
entries.4444: πύργος PU/RGOS pýrgos poor'-gos apparently a primary word ("burgh"); a tower or castle:--tower.
entries.4445: πυρέσσω PURE/SSW pyréssō poo-res'-so from G4443; to be on fire, i.e. (specially), to have a fever:--be sick of a fever.
entries.4446: πυρετός PURETO/S pyretós poo-ret-os' from G4445; inflamed, i.e. (by implication) feverish (as noun, fever):--fever.
entries.4447: πύρινος PU/RINOS pýrinos poo'-ree-nos from G4443; fiery, i.e. (by implication) flaming:--of fire.
entries.4448: πυρόω PURO/W pyróō poo-ro'-o from G4442; to kindle, i.e. (passively) to be ignited, glow (literally), be refined (by implication), or (figuratively) to be inflamed (with anger, grief, lust):--burn, fiery, be on fire, try.
entries.4449: πυῤῥάζω PUR)R(A/ZW pyrrházō poor-hrad'-zo from G4450; to redden (intransitively):--be red.
entries.4450: πυῤῥός PUR)R(O/S pyrrhós poor-hros' from G4442; fire-like, i.e. (specially), flame- colored:--red.
entries.4451: πύρωσις PU/RWSIS pýrōsis poo'-ro-sis from G4448; ignition, i.e. (specially), smelting (figuratively, conflagration, calamity as a test):--burning, trial.
entries.4452: ‐πω -PW -pō -po another form of the base of G4458; an enclitic particle of indefiniteness; yet, even; used only in the compounds. See G3369, G3380, G3764, G3768, G4455.
entries.4453: πωλέω PWLE/W pōléō po-leh'-o probably ultimately from πέλομαι PE/LOMAI pélomai (to be busy, to trade); to barter (as a pedlar), i.e. to sell:--sell, whatever is sold.
entries.4454: πῶλος PW=LOS pōlos po'-los apparently a primary word; a "foal" or "filly", i.e. (specially), a young ass:--colt.
entries.4455: πώποτε PW/POTE pṓpote po'-pot-e from G4452 and G4218; at any time, i.e. (with negative particle) at no time:--at any time, + never (…to any man), + yet, never man.
entries.4456: πωρόω PWRO/W pōróō po-ro'-o apparently from πῶρος PW=ROS pōros (a kind of stone); to petrify, i.e. (figuratively) to indurate (render stupid or callous):-- blind, harden.
entries.4457: πώρωσις PW/RWSIS pṓrōsis po'-ro-sis from G4456; stupidity or callousness:--blindness, hardness.
entries.4458: ‐πώς -PW/S -pṓs poce adverb from the base of G4225; an enclitic particle of indefiniteness of manner; somehow or anyhow; used only in composition:--haply, by any (some) means, perhaps. See G1513, G3381. Compare G4459.
entries.4459: πῶς PW=S pōs poce adverb from the base of G4226; an interrogative particle of manner; in what way? (sometimes the question is indirect, how?); also as exclamation, how much!:--how, after (by) what manner (means), that. (Occasionally unexpressed in English).
entries.4460: Ῥαάβ *(RAA/B Rhaáb hrah-ab' of Hebrew origin (H7343); Raab (i.e. Rachab), a Canaanitess:--Rahab. See also G4477.
entries.4461: ῥαββί R(ABBI/ rhabbí hrab-bee' of Hebrew origin (H07227 with pronominal suffix); my master, i.e Rabbi, as an official title of honor:--Master, Rabbi.
entries.4462: ῥαββονί R(ABBONI/ rhabboní hrab-bon-ee' , or ῥαββουνί R(ABBOUNI/ rhabbouní hrab-boo-nee' of Chaldee origin; corresponding to G4461:--Lord, Rabboni.
entries.4463: ῥαβδίζω R(ABDI/ZW rhabdízō hrab-did'-zo from G4464; to strike with a stick, i.e. bastinado:--beat (with rods).
entries.4464: ῥάβδος R(A/BDOS rhábdos hrab'-dos from the base of G4474; a stick or wand (as a cudgel, a cane or a baton of royalty):--rod, sceptre, staff.
entries.4465: ῥαβδοῦχος R(ABDOU=XOS rhabdoûchos hrab-doo'-khos from G4464 and G2192; a rod- (the Latin fasces) holder, i.e. a Roman lictor (constable or executioner):--serjeant.
entries.4466: Ῥαγαῦ *(RAGAU= Rhagaû hrag-ow' of Hebrew origin (H07466); Ragau (i.e. Reu), a patriarch:--Ragau.
entries.4467: ῥᾳδιούργημα R(A|DIOU/RGHMA rhaidioúrgēma hrad-ee-oorg'-ay-mah from a compound of ῥᾴδιος R(A/|DIOS rháidios (easy, i.e. reckless) and G2041; easy-going behavior, i.e. (by extension) a crime:--lewdness.
entries.4468: ῥᾳδιουργία R(A|DIOURGI/A rhaidiourgía hrad-ee-oorg-ee'-a from the same as G4467; recklessness, i.e. (by extension) malignity:--mischief.
entries.4469: ῥακά R(AKA/ rhaká rhak-ah' of Chaldee origin (compare H07386); O empty one, i.e. thou worthless (as a term of utter vilification):--Raca.
entries.4470: ῥάκος R(A/KOS rhákos hrak'-os from G4486; a "rag," i.e. piece of cloth:--cloth.
entries.4471: Ῥαμᾶ *(RAMA= Rhamâ hram-ah' of Hebrew origin (H07414); Rama (i.e. Ramah), a place in Palestine:--Rama.
entries.4472: ῥαντίζω R(ANTI/ZW rhantízō hran-tid'-zo from a derivative of ῥαίνω R(AI/NW rhaínō (to sprinkle); o render besprinkled, i.e. asperse (ceremonially or figuratively):-- sprinkle.
entries.4473: ῥαντισμός R(ANTISMO/S rhantismós hran-tis-mos' from G4472; aspersion (ceremonially or figuratively):--sprinkling.
entries.4474: ῥαπίζω R(API/ZW rhapízō hrap-id'-zo from a derivative of a primary ῥέπω R(E/PW rhépō (to let fall, "rap"); to slap:--smite (with the palm of the hand). Compare G5180.
entries.4475: ῥάπισμα R(A/PISMA rhápisma hrap'-is-mah from G4474; a slap:--(+ strike with the) palm of the hand, smite with the hand.
entries.4476: ῥαφίς R(AFI/S rhaphís hraf-ece' from a primary ῥάπτω R(A/PTW rháptō (to sew; perhaps rather akin to the base of G4474 through the idea of puncturing); a needle:-- needle.
entries.4477: Ῥαχάβ *(RAXA/B Rhacháb hrakh-ab' from the same as G4460; Rachab, a Canaanitess:--Rachab.
entries.4478: Ῥαχήλ *(RAXH/L Rhachḗl hrakh-ale' of Hebrew origin (H07354); Rachel, the wife of Jacob:--Rachel.
entries.4479: Ῥεβέκκα *(REBE/KKA Rhebékka hreb-bek'-kah of Hebrew origin (H07259); Rebecca (i.e. Ribkah), the wife of Isaac:--Rebecca.
entries.4480: ῥέδα R(E/DA rhéda hred'-ah of Latin origin; a rheda, i.e. four-wheeled carriage (wagon for riding):--chariot.
entries.4481: Ῥεμφάν *(REMFA/N Rhemphán hrem-fan' by incorrect transliteration for a word of Hebrew origin (H03594); Remphan (i.e. Kijun), an Egyptian idol:--Remphan.
entries.4482: ῥέω R(E/W rhéō hreh'-o a primary verb; for some tenses of which a prolonged form ῥεύω R(EU/W rheúō hryoo'-o is used to flow ("run"; as water):--flow.
entries.4483: ῥέω R(E/W rhéō hreh'-o , for certain tenses of which a prolonged form ἐρέω E)RE/W eréō er-eh'-o is used; and both as alternate for G2036 perhaps akin (or identical) with G4482 (through the idea of pouring forth); to utter, i.e. speak or say:--command, make, say, speak (of). Compare G3004.
entries.4484: Ῥήγιον *(RH/GION Rhḗgion hrayg'-ee-on of Latin origin; Rhegium, a place in Italy:--Rhegium.
entries.4485: ῥῆγμα R(H=GMA rhēgma hrayg'-mah from G4486; something torn, i.e. a fragment (by implication and abstractly, a fall):--ruin.
entries.4486: ῥήγνυμι R(H/GNUMI rhḗgnymi hrayg'-noo-mee or ῥήσσω R(H/SSW rhḗssō hrace'-so both prolonged forms of ῥήκω R(H/KW rhḗkō (which appears only in certain forms, and is itself probably a strengthened form of ἄγνυμι A)/GNUMI ágnymi (see in G2608)); to "break," "wreck" or "crack", i.e. (especially) to sunder (by separation of the parts; G2608 being its intensive (with the preposition in composition), and G2352 a shattering to minute fragments; but not a reduction to the constituent particles, like G3089) or disrupt, lacerate; by implication, to convulse (with spasms); figuratively, to give vent to joyful emotions:--break (forth), burst, rend, tear.
entries.4487: ῥῆμα R(H=MA rhēma hray'-mah from G4483; an utterance (individually, collectively or specially),; by implication, a matter or topic (especially of narration, command or dispute); with a negative naught whatever:--+ evil, + nothing, saying, word.
entries.4488: Ῥησά *(RHSA/ Rhēsá hray-sah' probably of Hebrew origin (apparently for H07509); Resa (i.e. Rephajah), an Israelite:--Rhesa.
entries.4489: ῥήτωρ R(H/TWR rhḗtōr hray'-tore from G4483; a speaker, i.e. (by implication) a forensic advocate:--orator.
entries.4490: ῥητῶς R(HTW=S rhētōs hray-toce' adverb from a derivative of G4483; out-spokenly, i.e. distinctly:--expressly.
entries.4491: ῥίζα R(I/ZA rhíza hrid'-zah apparently a primary word; a "root" (literally or figuratively):--root.
entries.4492: ῥιζόω R(IZO/W rhizóō hrid-zo'-o from G4491; to root (figuratively, become stable):--root.
entries.4493: ῥιπή R(IPH/ rhipḗ hree-pay' from G4496; a jerk (of the eye, i.e. (by analogy) an instant):--twinkling.
entries.4494: ῥιπίζω R(IPI/ZW rhipízō hrip-id'-zo from a derivative of G4496 (meaning a fan or bellows); to breeze up, i.e. (by analogy) to agitate (into waves):--toss.
entries.4495: ῥιπτέω R(IPTE/W rhiptéō hrip-teh'-o from a derivative of G4496; to toss up:--cast off.
entries.4496: ῥίπτω R(I/PTW rhíptō hrip'-to a primary verb (perhaps rather akin to the base of G4474, through the idea of sudden motion); to fling (properly, with a quick toss, thus differing from G906, which denotes a deliberate hurl; and from τείνω TEI/NW teínō (see in G1614), which indicates an extended projection); by qualification, to deposit (as if a load); by extension, to disperse:--cast (down, out), scatter abroad, throw.
entries.4497: Ῥοβοάμ *(ROBOA/M Rhoboám hrob-o-am' of Hebrew origin (H07346); Roboam (i.e. Rechobam), an Israelite:--Roboam.
entries.4498: Ῥόδη *(RO/DH Rhódē hrod'-ay probably for rhode (a rose); Rode, a servant girl:--Rhoda.
entries.4499: Ῥόδος *(RO/DOS Rhódos hrod'-os probably from ῥόδον R(O/DON rhódon (a rose); Rhodus, an island of the Mediterranean:--Rhodes.
entries.4500: ῥοιζηδόν R(OIZHDO/N rhoizēdón hroyd-zay-don' adverb from a derivative of ῥοῖζος R(OI=ZOS rhoîzos (a whir); whizzingly, i.e. with a crash:--with a great noise.
entries.4501: ῥομφαία R(OMFAI/A rhomphaía hrom-fah'-yah probably of foreign origin; a sabre, i.e. a long and broad cutlass (any weapon of the kind, literally or figuratively):--sword.
entries.4502: Ῥουβήν *(ROUBH/N Rhoubḗn hroo-bane' of Hebrew origin (H07205); Ruben (i.e. Reuben), an Israelite:--Reuben.
entries.4503: Ῥούθ *(ROU/Q Rhoúth hrooth of Hebrew origin (H07327); Ruth, a Moabitess:--Ruth.
entries.4504: Ῥοῦφος *(ROU=FOS Rhoûphos hroo'-fos of Latin origin; red; Rufus, a Christian:--Rufus.
entries.4505: ῥύμη R(U/MH rhýmē hroo'-may prolongation from G4506 in its original sense; an alley or avenue (as crowded):--lane, street.
entries.4506: ῥύομαι R(U/OMAI rhýomai rhoo'-om-ahee middle voice of an obsolete verb, akin to G4482 (through the idea of a current; compare G4511); to rush or draw (for oneself), i.e. rescue:--deliver(-er).
entries.4507: ῥυπαρία R(UPARI/A rhyparía hroo-par-ee'-ah from G4508; dirtiness (morally):--turpitude.
entries.4508: ῥυπαρός R(UPARO/S rhyparós rhoo-par-os' from G4509; dirty, i.e. (relatively) cheap or shabby; morally, wicked:--vile.
entries.4509: ῥύπος R(U/POS rhýpos hroo'-pos of uncertain affinity; dirt, i.e. (morally) depravity:--filth.
entries.4510: ῥυπόω R(UPO/W rhypóō rhoo-po'-o from G4509; to soil, i.e. (intransitively) to become dirty (morally):--be filthy.
entries.4511: ῥύσις R(U/SIS rhýsis hroo'-sis from G4506 in the sense of its congener G4482; a flux (of blood):--issue.
entries.4512: ῥυτίς R(UTI/S rhytís hroo-tece' from G4506; a fold (as drawing together), i.e. a wrinkle (especially on the face):--wrinkle.
entries.4513: Ῥωμαϊκός *(RWMAI+KO/S Rhōmaïkós rho-mah-ee-kos' from G4514; Romaic, i.e. Latin:--Latin.
entries.4514: Ῥωμαῖος *(RWMAI=OS Rhōmaîos hro-mah'-yos from G4516; Romæan, i.e. Roman (as noun):--Roman, of Rome.
entries.4515: Ῥωμαϊστί *(RWMAI+STI/ Rhōmaïstí hro-mah-is-tee' adverb from a presumed derivative of G4516; Romaistically, i.e. in the Latin language:--Latin.
entries.4516: Ῥώμη *(RW/MH Rhṓmē hro'-may from the base of G4517; strength; Roma, the capital of Italy:--Rome.
entries.4517: ῥώννυμι R(W/NNUMI rhṓnnymi hrone'-noo-mee prolongation from ῥώομαι R(W/OMAI rhṓomai (to dart; probably akin to G4506); to strengthen, i.e. (impersonal passive) have health (as a parting exclamation, good-bye):--farewell.
entries.4518: σαβαχθάνι SABAXQA/NI sabachtháni sab-akh-than-ee' of Chaldee or (H07662 with pronominal suffix); thou hast left me; sabachthani (i.e. shebakthani), a cry of distress:--sabachthani.
entries.4519: σαβαώθ SABAW/Q sabaṓth sab-ah-owth' of Hebrew origin (H06635 in feminine plural); armies; sabaoth (i.e. tsebaoth), a military epithet of God:--sabaoth.
entries.4520: σαββατισμός SABBATISMO/S sabbatismós sab-bat-is-mos' from a derivative of G4521; a "sabbatism", i.e. (figuratively) the repose of Christianity (as a type of heaven):--rest.
entries.4521: σάββατον SA/BBATON sábbaton sab'-bat-on of Hebrew origin (H07676); the Sabbath (i.e. Shabbath), or day of weekly repose from secular avocations (also the observance or institution itself); by extension, a se'nnight, i.e. the interval between two Sabbaths; likewise the plural in all the above applications:--sabbath (day), week.
entries.4522: σαγήνη SAGH/NH sagḗnē sag-ay'-nay from a derivative of σάττω SA/TTW sáttō (to equip) meaning furniture, especially a pack-saddle (which in the East is merely a bag of netted rope); a "seine" for fishing:--net.
entries.4523: Σαδδουκαῖος *SADDOUKAI=OS Saddoukaîos sad-doo-kah'-yos probably from G4524; a Sadducæan (i.e. Tsadokian), or follower of a certain heretical Israelite:--Sadducee.
entries.4524: Σαδώκ *SADW/K Sadṓk sad-oke' of Hebrew origin (H06659); Sadoc (i.e. Tsadok), an Israelite:--Sadoc.
entries.4525: σαίνω SAI/NW saínō sah'-ee-no akin to G4579; to wag (as a dog its tail fawningly), i.e. (generally) to shake (figuratively, disturb):--move.
entries.4526: σάκκος SA/KKOS sákkos sak'-kos of Hebrew origin (H08242); "sack"-cloth, i.e. mohair (the material or garments made of it, worn as a sign of grief):-- sackcloth.
entries.4527: Σαλά *SALA/ Salá sal-ah' of Hebrew origin (H07974); Sala (i.e. Shelach), a patriarch :--Sala.
entries.4528: Σαλαθιήλ *SALAQIH/L Salathiḗl sal-ath-ee-ale' of Hebrew origin (H07597); Salathiel (i.e. Shealtiel), an Israelite:--Salathiel.
entries.4529: Σαλαμίς *SALAMI/S Salamís sal-am-ece' probably from G4535 (from the surge on the shore); Salamis, a place in Cyprus:--Salamis.
entries.4530: Σαλείμ *SALEI/M Saleím sal-ime' probably from the same as G4531; Salim, a place in Palestine:--Salim.
entries.4531: σαλεύω SALEU/W saleúō sal-yoo'-o from G4535; to waver, i.e. agitate, rock, topple or (by implication) destroy; figuratively, to disturb, incite:--move, shake (together), which can(-not) be shaken, stir up.
entries.4532: Σαλήμ *SALH/M Salḗm sal-ame' of Hebrew origin (H08004); Salem (i.e. Shalem), a place in Palestine:--Salem.
entries.4533: Σαλμών *SALMW/N Salmṓn sal-mone' of Hebrew origin (H08012); Salmon, an Israelite:--Salmon.
entries.4534: Σαλμώνη *SALMW/NH Salmṓnē sal-mo'-nay perhaps of similar origin to G4529; Salmone, a place in Crete:--Salmone.
entries.4535: σάλος SA/LOS sálos sal'-os probably from the base of G4525; a vibration, i.e. (specially), billow:--wave.
entries.4536: σάλπιγξ SA/LPIGC sálpinx sal'-pinx perhaps from G4535 (through the idea of quavering or reverberation); a trumpet:--trump(-et).
entries.4537: σαλπίζω SALPI/ZW salpízō sal-pid'-zo from G4536; to trumpet, i.e. sound a blast (literally or figuratively):--(which are yet to) sound (a trumpet).
entries.4538: σαλπιστής SALPISTH/S salpistḗs sal-pis-tace' from G4537; a trumpeter:--trumpeter.
entries.4539: Σαλώμη *SALW/MH Salṓmē sal-o'-may probably of Hebrew origin (feminine from H07965); Salome (i.e. Shelomah), an Israelitess:--Salome.
entries.4540: Σαμάρεια *SAMA/REIA Samáreia sam-ar'-i-ah of Hebrew origin (H08111); Samaria (i.e. Shomeron), a city and region of Palestine:--Samaria.
entries.4541: Σαμαρείτης *SAMAREI/THS Samareítēs sam-ar-i'-tace from G4540; a Samarite, i.e. inhabitant of Samaria:--Samaritan.
entries.4542: Σαμαρεῖτις *SAMAREI=TIS Samareîtis sam-ar-i'-tis feminine of G4541; a Samaritess, i.e. woman of Samaria:--of Samaria.
entries.4543: Σαμοθρᾴκη *SAMOQRA/|KH Samothráikē sam-oth-rak'-ay from G4544 and Θτρᾴκη *QTRA/|KH Thtráikē (Thrace); Samo-thrace (Samos of Thrace), an island in the Mediterranean:--Samothracia.
entries.4544: Σάμος *SA/MOS Sámos sam'-os of uncertain affinity; Samus, an island of the Mediterranean:--Samos.
entries.4545: Σαμουήλ *SAMOUH/L Samouḗl sam-oo-ale' of Hebrew origin (H08050); Samuel (i.e. Shemuel), an Israelite:--Samuel.
entries.4546: Σαμψών *SAMYW/N Sampsṓn samp-sone' of Hebrew origin (H08123); Sampson (i.e. Shimshon), an Israelite:--Samson.
entries.4547: σανδάλιον SANDA/LION sandálion san-dal'-ee-on neuter of a derivative of σάνδαλον SA/NDALON sándalon (a "sandal"; of uncertain origin); a slipper or sole-pad:--sandal.
entries.4548: σανίς SANI/S sanís san-ece' of uncertain affinity; a plank:--board.
entries.4549: Σαούλ *SAOU/L Saoúl sah-ool' of Hebrew origin (H07586); Saul (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul:--Saul. Compare G4569.
entries.4550: σαπρός SAPRO/S saprós sap-ros' from G4595; rotten, i.e. worthless (literally or morally):--bad, corrupt. Compare G4190.
entries.4551: Σαπφείρη *SAPFEI/RH Sappheírē sap-fi'-ray feminine of G4552; Sapphire, an Israelitess:--Sapphira.
entries.4552: σάπφειρος SA/PFEIROS sáppheiros sap'-fi-ros of Hebrew origin (H05601); a "sapphire" or lapis-lazuli gem:--sapphire.
entries.4553: σαργάνη SARGA/NH sargánē sar-gan'-ay apparently of Hebrew origin (H08276); a basket (as interwoven or wicker-work:--basket.
entries.4554: Σάρδεις *SA/RDEIS Sárdeis sar'-dice plural of uncertain derivation; Sardis, a place in Asia Minor:--Sardis.
entries.4555: σάρδινος SA/RDINOS sárdinos sar'-dee-nos from the same as G4556; sardine (G3037 being implied), i.e. a gem, so called:--sardine.
entries.4556: σάρδιος SA/RDIOS sárdios sar'-dee-os properly, an adjective from an uncertain base; sardian (3037 being implied), i.e. (as noun) the gem so called:--sardius.
entries.4557: σαρδόνυξ SARDO/NUC sardónyx sar-don'-oox from the base of G4556 and ὄνυξ O)/NUC ónyx (the nail of a finger; hence the "onyx" stone); a "sardonyx", i.e. the gem so called:-- sardonyx.
entries.4558: Σάρεπτα *SA/REPTA Sárepta sar'-ep-tah of Hebrew origin (H06886); Sarepta (i.e. Tsarephath), a place in Palestine:--Sarepta.
entries.4559: σαρκικός SARKIKO/S sarkikós sar-kee-kos' from G4561; pertaining to flesh, i.e. (by extension) bodily, temporal, or (by implication) animal, unregenerate:--carnal, fleshly.
entries.4560: σάρκινος SA/RKINOS sárkinos sar'-kee-nos from G4561; similar to flesh, i.e. (by analogy) soft:--fleshly.
entries.4561: σάρξ SA/RC sárx sarx probably from the base of G4563; flesh (as stripped of the skin), i.e. (strictly) the meat of an animal (as food), or (by extension) the body (as opposed to the soul (or spirit), or as the symbol of what is external, or as the means of kindred), or (by implication) human nature (with its frailties (physically or morally) and passions), or (specially), a human being (as such):--carnal(-ly, + -ly minded), flesh(-ly).
entries.4562: Σαρούχ *SAROU/X Saroúch sar-ooch' of Hebrew origin (H08286); Saruch (i.e. Serug), a patriarch:--Saruch.
entries.4563: σαρόω SARO/W saróō sar-o'-o from a derivative of σαίρω SAI/RW saírō (to brush off; akin to G4951); meaning a broom; to sweep:--sweep.
entries.4564: Σάῤῥα *SA/R)R(A Sárrha sar'-hrah of Hebrew origin (H08283); Sarra (i.e. Sarah), the wife of Abraham:--Sara, Sarah.
entries.4565: Σάρων *SA/RWN Sárōn sar'-one of Hebrew origin (H08289); Saron (i.e. Sharon), a district of Palestine:--Saron.
entries.4566: Σατᾶν *SATA=N Satân sat-an' of Hebrew origin (H07854); Satan, i.e. the devil:--Satan. Compare G4567.
entries.4567: Σατανᾶς *SATANA=S Satanâs sat-an-as' of Chaldee origin corresponding to H04566 (with the definite affix); the accuser, i.e. the devil:--Satan.
entries.4568: σάτον SA/TON sáton sat'-on of Hebrew origin (H05429); a certain measure for things dry:--measure.
entries.4569: Σαῦλος *SAU=LOS Saûlos sow'-los of Hebrew origin, the same as G4549; Saulus (i.e. Shaul), the Jewish name of Paul:--Saul.
entries.4570: σβέννυμι SBE/NNUMI sbénnymi sben'-noo-mee a prolonged form of an apparently primary verb; to extinguish (literally or figuratively):--go out, quench.
entries.4571: σέ SE/ sé seh accusative case singular of G4771; thee:--thee, thou, X thy house.
entries.4572: σεαυτοῦ SEAUTOU= seautoû seh-ow-too' ; genitive case from G4571 and G846, also dative case of the same, σεαυτῷ SEAUTW=| seautōi seh-ow-to' , and accusative case σεαυτόν SEAUTO/N seautón seh-ow-ton' , likewise contracted σαυτοῦ SAUTOU= sautoû sow-too' , σαυτῷ SAUTW=| sautōi sow-to' , and σαυτόν SAUTO/N sautón sow-ton' , respectively; of (with, to) thyself:--thee, thine own self, (thou) thy(-self).
entries.4573: σεβάζομαι SEBA/ZOMAI sebázomai seb-ad'-zom-ahee middle voice from a derivative of G4576; to venerate, i.e. adore:--worship.
entries.4574: σέβασμα SE/BASMA sébasma seb'-as-mah from G4573; something adored, i.e. an object of worship (god, altar, etc):--devotion, that is worshipped.
entries.4575: σεβαστός SEBASTO/S sebastós seb-as-tos' from G4573; venerable (august), i.e. (as noun) a title of the Roman Emperor, or (as adjective) imperial:--Augustus(-').
entries.4576: σέβομαι SE/BOMAI sébomai seb'-om-ahee middle voice of an apparently primary verb; to revere, i.e. adore:--devout, religious, worship.
entries.4577: σειρά SEIRA/ seirá si-rah' probably from G4951 through its congener εἴρω EI)/RW eírō (to fasten; akin to G138); a chain (as binding or drawing):--chain.
entries.4578: σεισμός SEISMO/S seismós sice-mos' from G4579; a commotion, i.e. (of the air) a gale, (of the ground) an earthquake:--earthquake, tempest.
entries.4579: σείω SEI/W seíō si'-o apparently a primary verb; to rock (vibrate, properly, sideways or to and fro), i.e. (generally) to agitate (in any direction; cause to tremble); figuratively, to throw into a tremor (of fear or concern):--move, quake, shake.
entries.4580: Σεκοῦνδος *SEKOU=NDOS Sekoûndos sek-oon'-dos of Latin origin; "second"; Secundus, a Christian:--Secundus.
entries.4581: Σελεύκεια *SELEU/KEIA Seleúkeia sel-yook'-i-ah from Σέλευκος *SE/LEUKOS Séleukos (Seleucus, a Syrian king); Seleuceia, a place in Syria:--Seleucia.
entries.4582: σελήνη SELH/NH selḗnē sel-ay'-nay from σέλας SE/LAS sélas (brilliancy; probably akin to the alternate of G138, through the idea of attractiveness); the moon:--moon.
entries.4583: σεληνιάζομαι SELHNIA/ZOMAI selēniázomai sel-ay-nee-ad'-zom-ahee middle voice or passive from a presumed derivative of G4582; to be moon-struck, i.e. crazy:--be a lunatic.
entries.4584: Σεμεΐ *SEMEI/+ Semeḯ sem-eh-ee' of Hebrew origin (H08096); Semei (i.e. Shimi), an Israelite:--Semei.
entries.4585: σεμίδαλις SEMI/DALIS semídalis sem-id'-al-is probably of foreign origin; fine wheaten flour:--fine flour.
entries.4586: σεμνός SEMNO/S semnós sem-nos' from G4576; venerable, i.e. honorable:--grave, honest.
entries.4587: σεμνότης SEMNO/THS semnótēs sem-not'-ace from G4586; venerableness, i.e. probity:--gravity, honesty.
entries.4588: Σέργιος *SE/RGIOS Sérgios serg'-ee-os of Latin origin; Sergius, a Roman:--Sergius.
entries.4589: Σήθ *SH/Q Sḗth sayth of Hebrew origin (H08352); Seth (i.e. Sheth), a patriarch:--Seth.
entries.4590: Σήμ *SH/M Sḗm same of Hebrew origin (H08035); Sem (i.e. Shem), a patriarch:-- Sem.
entries.4591: σημαίνω SHMAI/NW sēmaínō say-mah'-ee-no from σῆμα SH=MA sēma (a mark; of uncertain derivation); to indicate:--signify.
entries.4592: σημεῖον SHMEI=ON sēmeîon say-mi'-on neuter of a presumed derivative of the base of G4591; an indication, especially ceremonially or supernaturally:--miracle, sign, token, wonder.
entries.4593: σημειόω SHMEIO/W sēmeióō say-mi-o'-o from G4592; to distinguish, i.e. mark (for avoidance):--note.
entries.4594: σήμερον SH/MERON sḗmeron say'-mer-on neuter (as adverb) of a presumed compound of the article G3588 (t changed to s) and G2250; on the (i.e. this) day (or night current or just passed); generally, now (i.e. at present, hitherto):--this (to-)day.
entries.4595: σήπω SH/PW sḗpō say'-po apparently a primary verb; to putrefy, i.e. (figuratively) perish:--be corrupted.
entries.4596: σηρικός SHRIKO/S sērikós say-ree-kos' from Σήρ *SH/R Sḗr (an Indian tribe from whom silk was procured; hence the name of the silk-worm); Seric, i.e. silken (neuter as noun, a silky fabric):--silk.
entries.4597: σής SH/S sḗs sace apparently of Hebrew origin (H05580); a moth:--moth.
entries.4598: σητόβρωτος SHTO/BRWTOS sētóbrōtos say-tob'-ro-tos from G4597 and a derivative of G977; moth-eaten:--motheaten.
entries.4599: σθενόω SQENO/W sthenóō sthen-o'-o from σθένος SQE/NOS sthénos (bodily vigor; probably akin to the base of G2476); to strengthen, i.e. (figuratively) confirm (in spiritual knowledge and power):--strengthen.
entries.4600: σιαγών SIAGW/N siagṓn see-ag-one' of uncertain derivation; the jaw-bone, i.e. (by implication) the cheek or side of the face:--cheek.
entries.4601: σιγάω SIGA/W sigáō see-gah'-o from G4602; to keep silent (transitively or intransitively):--keep close (secret, silence), hold peace.
entries.4602: σιγή SIGH/ sigḗ see-gay' apparently from σίζω SI/ZW sízō (to hiss, i.e. hist or hush); silence:--silence. Compare G4623.
entries.4603: σιδήρεος SIDH/REOS sidḗreos sid-ay'-reh-os from G4604; made of iron:--(of) iron.
entries.4604: σίδηρος SI/DHROS sídēros sid'-ay-ros of uncertain derivation; iron:--iron.
entries.4605: Σιδών *SIDW/N Sidṓn sid-one' of Hebrew origin (H06721); Sidon (i.e. Tsidon), a place in Palestine:--Sidon.
entries.4606: Σιδώνιος *SIDW/NIOS Sidṓnios sid-o'-nee-os from G4605; a Sidonian, i.e. inhabitant of Sidon:--of Sidon.
entries.4607: σικάριος SIKA/RIOS sikários sik-ar'-ee-os of Latin origin; a dagger-man or assassin; a freebooter (Jewish fanatic outlawed by the Romans):--murderer. Compare G5406.
entries.4608: σίκερα SI/KERA síkera sik'-er-ah of Hebrew origin (H07941); an intoxicant, i.e. intensely fermented liquor:--strong drink.
entries.4609: Σίλας *SI/LAS Sílas see'-las contraction for G4610; Silas, a Christian:--Silas.
entries.4610: Σιλουανός *SILOUANO/S Silouanós sil-oo-an-os' of Latin origin; "silvan"; Silvanus, a Christian:--Silvanus. Compare G4609.
entries.4611: Σιλωάμ *SILWA/M Silōám sil-o-am' of Hebrew origin (H07975); Siloam (i.e. Shiloach), a pool of Jerusalem:--Siloam.
entries.4612: σιμικίνθιον SIMIKI/NQION simikínthion sim-ee-kin'-thee-on of Latin origin; a semicinctium or half-girding, i.e. narrow covering (apron):--apron.
entries.4613: Σίμων *SI/MWN Símōn see'-mone of Hebrew origin (H08095); Simon (i.e. Shimon), the name of nine Israelites:--Simon. Compare G4826.
entries.4614: Σινᾶ *SINA= Sinâ see-nah' of Hebrew origin (H05514); Sina (i.e. Sinai), a mountain in Arabia:--Sina.
entries.4615: σίναπι SI/NAPI sínapi sin'-ap-ee perhaps from σίνομαι SI/NOMAI sínomai (to hurt, i.e. sting); mustard (the plant):--mustard.
entries.4616: σινδών SINDW/N sindṓn sin-done' of uncertain (perhaps foreign) origin; byssos, i.e. bleached linen (the cloth or a garment of it):--(fine) linen (cloth).
entries.4617: σινιάζω SINIA/ZW siniázō sin-ee-ad'-zo from σινίον SINI/ON siníon (a sieve); to riddle (figuratively):--sift.
entries.4618: σιτευτός SITEUTO/S siteutós sit-yoo-ros' from a derivative of G4621; grain-fed, i.e. fattened:--fatted.
entries.4619: σιτιστός SITISTO/S sitistós sit-is-tos' from a derivative of G4621; grained, i.e. fatted:--fatling.
entries.4620: σιτόμετρον SITO/METRON sitómetron sit-om'-et-ron from G4621 and G3358; a grain-measure, i.e. (by implication) ration (allowance of food):--portion of meat.
entries.4621: σῖτος SI=TOS sîtos see'-tos , also plural irregular neuter σῖτα SI=TA sîta see'-tah of uncertain derivation; grain, especially wheat:--corn, wheat.
entries.4622: Σιών *SIW/N Siṓn see-own' of Hebrew origin (H06726); Sion (i.e. Tsijon), a hill of Jerusalem; figuratively, the Church (militant or triumphant):--Sion.
entries.4623: σιωπάω SIWPA/W siōpáō see-o-pah'-o from σιωπή SIWPH/ siōpḗ (silence, i.e. a hush; properly, muteness, i.e. involuntary stillness, or inability to speak; and thus differing from G4602, which is rather a voluntary refusal or indisposition to speak, although the terms are often used synonymously); to be dumb (but not deaf also, like 2974 properly); figuratively, to be calm (as quiet water):--dumb, (hold) peace.
entries.4624: σκανδαλίζω SKANDALI/ZW skandalízō skan-dal-id'-zo from G4625; to entrap, i.e. trip up (figuratively, stumble (transitively) or entice to sin, apostasy or displeasure):--(make to) offend.
entries.4625: σκάνδαλον SKA/NDALON skándalon skan'-dal-on ("scandal"); probably from a derivative of G2578; a trap-stick (bent sapling), i.e. snare (figuratively, cause of displeasure or sin):--occasion to fall (of stumbling), offence, thing that offends, stumblingblock.
entries.4626: σκάπτω SKA/PTW skáptō skap'-to apparently a primary verb; to dig:--dig.
entries.4627: σκάφη SKA/FH skáphē skaf'-ay a "skiff" (as if dug out), or yawl (carried aboard a large vessel for landing):--boat.
entries.4628: σκέλος SKE/LOS skélos skel'-os apparently from σκέλλω SKE/LLW skéllō (to parch; through the idea of leanness); the leg (as lank):--leg.
entries.4629: σκέπασμα SKE/PASMA sképasma skep'-as-mah from a derivative of σκέπας SKE/PAS sképas (a covering; perhaps akin to the base of G4649 through the idea of noticeableness); clothing:--raiment.
entries.4630: Σκευᾶς *SKEUA=S Skeuâs skyoo-as' apparently of Latin origin; left-handed; Scevas (i.e. Scævus), an Israelite:--Sceva.
entries.4631: σκευή SKEUH/ skeuḗ skyoo-ay' from G4632; furniture, i.e. spare tackle:--tackling.
entries.4632: σκεῦος SKEU=OS skeûos skyoo'-os of uncertain affinity; a vessel, implement, equipment or apparatus (literally or figuratively [specially, a wife as contributing to the usefulness of the husband]):--goods, sail, stuff, vessel.
entries.4633: σκηνή SKHNH/ skēnḗ skay-nay' apparently akin to G4632 and G4639; a tent or cloth hut (literally or figuratively):--habitation, tabernacle.
entries.4634: σκηνοπηγία SKHNOPHGI/A skēnopēgía skay-nop-ayg-ee'-ah from G4636 and G4078; the Festival of Tabernacles (so called from the custom of erecting booths for temporary homes):--tabernacles.
entries.4635: σκηνοποιός SKHNOPOIO/S skēnopoiós skay-nop-oy-os' from G4633 and G4160; a manufacturer of tents:--tent-maker.
entries.4636: σκῆνος SKH=NOS skēnos skay'-nos from G4633; a hut or temporary residence, i.e. (figuratively) the human body (as the abode of the spirit):--tabernacle.
entries.4637: σκηνόω SKHNO/W skēnóō skay-no'-o from G4636; to tent or encamp, i.e. (figuratively) to occupy (as a mansion) or (specially), to reside (as God did in the Tabernacle of old, a symbol of protection and communion):-- dwell.
entries.4638: σκήνωμα SKH/NWMA skḗnōma skay'-no-mah from G4637; an encampment, i.e. (figuratively) the Temple (as God's residence), the body (as a tenement for the soul):-- tabernacle.
entries.4639: σκιά SKIA/ skiá skee'-ah apparently a primary word; "shade" or a shadow (literally or figuratively (darkness of error or an adumbration)):-- shadow.
entries.4640: σκιρτάω SKIRTA/W skirtáō skeer-tah'-o akin to σκαίρω SKAI/RW skaírō (to skip); to jump, i.e. sympathetically move (as the quickening of a fetus):--leap (for joy).
entries.4641: σκληροκαρδία SKLHROKARDI/A sklērokardía sklay-rok-ar-dee'-ah feminine of a compound of G4642 and G2588; hard-heartedness, i.e. (specially), destitution of (spiritual) perception:--hardness of heart.
entries.4642: σκληρός SKLHRO/S sklērós sklay-ros' from the base of G4628; dry, i.e. hard or tough (figuratively, harsh, severe):--fierce, hard.
entries.4643: σκληρότης SKLHRO/THS sklērótēs sklay-rot'-ace from G4642; callousness, i.e. (figuratively) stubbornness:--hardness.
entries.4644: σκληροτράχηλος SKLHROTRA/XHLOS sklērotráchēlos sklay-rot-rakh'-ay-los from G4642 and G5137; hardnaped, i.e. (figuratively) obstinate:--stiffnecked.
entries.4645: σκληρύνω SKLHRU/NW sklērýnō sklay-roo'-no from G4642; to indurate, i.e. (figuratively) render stubborn:--harden.
entries.4646: σκολιός SKOLIO/S skoliós skol-ee-os' from the base of G4628; warped, i.e. winding; figuratively, perverse:--crooked, froward, untoward.
entries.4647: σκόλοψ SKO/LOY skólops skol'-ops perhaps from the base of G4628 and G3700; withered at the front, i.e. a point or prickle (figuratively, a bodily annoyance or disability):--thorn.
entries.4648: σκοπέω SKOPE/W skopéō skop-eh'-o from G4649; to take aim at (spy), i.e. (figuratively) regard:--consider, take heed, look at (on), mark. Compare G3700.
entries.4649: σκοπός SKOPO/S skopós skop-os' from σκέπτομαι SKE/PTOMAI sképtomai (to peer about ("skeptic"); perhaps akin to G4626 through the idea of concealment; compare G4629); a watch (sentry or scout), i.e. (by implication) a goal:--mark.
entries.4650: σκορπίζω SKORPI/ZW skorpízō skor-pid'-zo apparently from the same as G4651 (through the idea of penetrating); to dissipate, i.e. (figuratively) put to flight, waste, be liberal:--disperse abroad, scatter (abroad).
entries.4651: σκορπίος SKORPI/OS skorpíos skor-pee'-os probably from an obsolete σκέρπω SKE/RPW skérpō (perhaps strengthened from the base of G4649 and meaning to pierce); a "scorpion" (from its sting):--scorpion.
entries.4652: σκοτεινός SKOTEINO/S skoteinós skot-i-nos' from G4655; opaque, i.e. (figuratively) benighted:--dark, full of darkness.
entries.4653: σκοτία SKOTI/A skotía skot-ee'-ah from G4655; dimness, obscurity (literally or figuratively):--dark(-ness).
entries.4654: σκοτίζω SKOTI/ZW skotízō skot-id-zo from G4655; to obscure (literally or figuratively):--darken.
entries.4655: σκότος SKO/TOS skótos skot'-os from the base of G4639; shadiness, i.e. obscurity (literally or figuratively):--darkness.
entries.4656: σκοτόω SKOTO/W skotóō skot-o'-o from G4655; to obscure or blind (literally or figuratively):--be full of darkness.
entries.4657: σκύβαλον SKU/BALON skýbalon skoo'-bal-on neuter of a presumed derivative of G1519 and G2965 and G906; what is thrown to the dogs, i.e. refuse (ordure):--dung.
entries.4658: Σκύθης *SKU/QHS Skýthēs skoo'-thace probably of foreign origin; a Scythene or Scythian, i.e. (by implication) a savage:--Scythian.
entries.4659: σκυθρωπός SKUQRWPO/S skythrōpós skoo-thro-pos' from σκυθρός SKUQRO/S skythrós (sullen) and a derivative of G3700; angry-visaged, i.e. gloomy or affecting a mournful appearance:--of a sad countenance.
entries.4660: σκύλλω SKU/LLW skýllō skool'-lo apparently a primary verb; to flay, i.e. (figuratively) to harass:--trouble(self).
entries.4661: σκῦλον SKU=LON skŷlon skoo'-lon neuter from G4660; something stripped (as a hide), i.e. booty:--spoil.
entries.4662: σκωληκόβρωτος SKWLHKO/BRWTOS skōlēkóbrōtos sko-lay-kob'-ro-tos from G4663 and a derivative of G977; worm-eaten, i.e. diseased with maggots:--eaten of worms.
entries.4663: σκώληξ SKW/LHC skṓlēx sko'-lakes of uncertain derivation; a grub, maggot or earth-worm:--worm.
entries.4664: σμαράγδινος SMARA/GDINOS smarágdinos smar-ag'-dee-nos from G4665; consisting of emerald:--emerald.
entries.4665: σμάραγδος SMA/RAGDOS smáragdos smar'-ag-dos of uncertain derivation; the emerald or green gem so called:--emerald.
entries.4666: σμύρνα SMU/RNA smýrna smoor'-nah apparently strengthened for G3464; myrrh:--myrrh.
entries.4667: Σμύρνα *SMU/RNA Smýrna smoor'-nah the same as G4666; Smyrna, a place in Asia Minor:--Smyrna.
entries.4668: Σμυρναῖος *SMURNAI=OS Smyrnaîos smoor-nah'-yos from G4667; a Smyrnæan:--in Smyrna.
entries.4669: σμυρνίζω SMURNI/ZW smyrnízō smoor-nid'-zo from G4667; to tincture with myrrh, i.e. embitter (as a narcotic):--mingle with myrrh.
entries.4670: Σόδομα *SO/DOMA Sódoma sod'-om-ah plural of Hebrew origin (H05467); Sodoma (i.e. Sedom), a place in Palestine:--Sodom.
entries.4671: σοί SOI/ soí soy dative case of G4771; to thee:--thee, thine own, thou, thy.
entries.4672: Σολομών *SOLOMW/N Solomṓn sol-om-one' of Hebrew origin (H08010); Solomon (i.e. Shelomoh), the son of David:--Solomon.
entries.4673: σορός SORO/S sorós sor-os' probably akin to the base of G4987; a funereal receptacle (urn, coffin), i.e. (by analogy) a bier:--bier.
entries.4674: σός SO/S sós sos from G4771; thine:--thine (own), thy (friend).
entries.4675: σοῦ SOU= soû soo genitive case of G4771; of thee, thy:--X home, thee, thine (own), thou, thy.
entries.4676: σουδάριον SOUDA/RION soudárion soo-dar'-ee-on of Latin origin; a sudarium (sweat-cloth), i.e. towel (for wiping the perspiration from the face, or binding the face of a corpse):--handkerchief, napkin.
entries.4677: Σουσάννα *SOUSA/NNA Sousánna soo-san'-nah of Hebrew origin (H07799 feminine); lily; Susannah (i.e. Shoshannah), an Israelitess:--Susanna.
entries.4678: σοφία SOFI/A sophía sof-ee'-ah from G4680; wisdom (higher or lower, worldly or spiritual):--wisdom.
entries.4679: σοφίζω SOFI/ZW sophízō sof-id'-zo from G4680; to render wise; in a sinister acceptation, to form "sophisms", i.e. continue plausible error:--cunningly devised, make wise.
entries.4680: σοφός SOFO/S sophós sof-os' akin to σαφής SAFH/S saphḗs (clear); wise (in a most general application):--wise. Compare G5429.
entries.4681: Σπανία *SPANI/A Spanía span-ee'-ah probably of foreign origin; Spania, a region of Europe:--Spain.
entries.4682: σπαράσσω SPARA/SSW sparássō spar-as'-so prolongation from σπαίρω SPAI/RW spaírō (to grasp; apparently strengthened from G4685 through the idea of spasmodic contraction); to mangle, i.e. convluse with epilepsy:--rend, tear.
entries.4683: σπαργανόω SPARGANO/W sparganóō spar-gan-o'-o from σπάργανον SPA/RGANON spárganon (a strip; from a derivative of the base of G4682 meaning to strap or wrap with strips); to swathe (an infant after the Oriental custom):--wrap in swaddling clothes.
entries.4684: σπαταλάω SPATALA/W spataláō spat-al-ah'-o from σπατάλη SPATA/LH spatálē (luxury); to be voluptuous:--live in pleasure, be wanton.
entries.4685: σπάω SPA/W spáō spah'-o a primary verb; to draw:--draw (out).
entries.4686: σπεῖρα SPEI=RA speîra spi'-rah of immediate Latin origin, but ultimately a derivative of G138 in the sense of its cognate G1507; a coil (spira, "spire"), i.e. (figuratively) a mass of men (a Roman military cohort; also (by analogy) a squad of Levitical janitors):--band.
entries.4687: σπείρω SPEI/RW speírō spi'-ro probably strengthened from G4685 (through the idea of extending); to scatter, i.e. sow (literally or figuratively):--sow(- er), receive seed.
entries.4688: σπεκουλάτωρ SPEKOULA/TWR spekoulátōr spek-oo-lat'-ore of Latin origin; a speculator, i.e. military scout (spy or (by extension) life-guardsman):--executioner.
entries.4689: σπένδω SPE/NDW spéndō spen'-do apparently a primary verb; to pour out as a libation, i.e. (figuratively) to devote (one's life or blood, as a sacrifice) ("spend"):--(be ready to) be offered.
entries.4690: σπέρμα SPE/RMA spérma sper'-mah from G4687; something sown, i.e. seed (including the male "sperm"); by implication, offspring; specially, a remnant (figuratively, as if kept over for planting):--issue, seed.
entries.4691: σπερμολόγος SPERMOLO/GOS spermológos sper-mol-og'-os from G4690 and G3004; a seed-picker (as the crow), i.e. (figuratively) a sponger, loafer (specially, a gossip or trifler in talk):--babbler.
entries.4692: σπεύδω SPEU/DW speúdō spyoo'-do probably strengthened from G4228; to "speed" ("study"), i.e. urge on (diligently or earnestly); by implication, to await eagerly:--(make, with) haste unto.
entries.4693: σπήλαιον SPH/LAION spḗlaion spay'-lah-yon neuter of a presumed derivative of σπέος SPE/OS spéos (a grotto); a cavern; by implication, a hiding-place or resort:--cave, den.
entries.4694: σπιλάς SPILA/S spilás spee-las' of uncertain derivation; a ledge or reef of rock in the sea:--spot (by confusion with G4696).
entries.4695: σπιλόω SPILO/W spilóō spee-lo'-o from G4696; to stain or soil (literally or figuratively):--defile, spot.
entries.4696: σπίλος SPI/LOS spílos spee'-los of uncertain derivation; a stain or blemish, i.e. (figuratively) defect, disgrace:--spot.
entries.4697: σπλαγχνίζομαι SPLAGXNI/ZOMAI splanchnízomai splangkh-nid'-zom-ahee middle voice from G4698; to have the bowels yearn, i.e. (figuratively) feel sympathy, to pity:--have (be moved with) compassion.
entries.4698: σπλάγχνον SPLA/GXNON splánchnon splangkh'-non probably strengthened from σπλήν SPLH/N splḗn (the "spleen"); an intestine (plural); figuratively, pity or sympathy:--bowels, inward affection, + tender mercy.
entries.4699: σπόγγος SPO/GGOS spóngos spong'-gos perhaps of foreign origin; a "sponge":--spunge.
entries.4700: σποδός SPODO/S spodós spod-os' of uncertain derivation; ashes:--ashes.
entries.4701: σπορά SPORA/ sporá spor-ah' from G4687; a sowing, i.e. (by implication) parentage:--seed.
entries.4702: σπόριμος SPO/RIMOS spórimos spor'-ee-mos from G4703; sown, i.e. (neuter plural) a planted field:--corn(-field).
entries.4703: σπόρος SPO/ROS spóros spro'-os from G4687; a scattering (of seed), i.e. (concretely) seed (as sown):--seed (X sown).
entries.4704: σπουδάζω SPOUDA/ZW spoudázō spoo-dad'-zo from G4710; to use speed, i.e. to make effort, be prompt or earnest:--do (give) diligence, be diligent (forward), endeavour, labour, study.
entries.4705: σπουδαῖος SPOUDAI=OS spoudaîos spoo-dah'-yos from G4710; prompt, energetic, earnest:--diligent.
entries.4706: σπουδαιότερον SPOUDAIO/TERON spoudaióteron spoo-dah-yot'-er-on neuter of G4707 as adverb; more earnestly than others), i.e. very promptly:--very diligently.
entries.4707: σπουδαιότερος SPOUDAIO/TEROS spoudaióteros spoo-dah-yot'-er-os comparative of G4705; more prompt, more earnest:--more diligent (forward).
entries.4708: σπουδαιοτέρως SPOUDAIOTE/RWS spoudaiotérōs spoo-dah-yot-er'-oce adverb from G4707; more speedily, i.e. sooner than otherwise:--more carefully.
entries.4709: σπουδαίως SPOUDAI/WS spoudaíōs spoo-dah'-yoce adverb from G4705; earnestly, promptly:--diligently, instantly.
entries.4710: σπουδή SPOUDH/ spoudḗ spoo-day' from G4692; "speed", i.e. (by implication) despatch, eagerness, earnestness:--business, (earnest) care(-fulness), diligence, forwardness, haste.
entries.4711: σπυρίς SPURI/S spyrís spoo-rece' from G4687 (as woven); a hamper or lunch-receptacle:--basket.
entries.4712: στάδιον STA/DION stádion stad'-ee-on , or masculine (in plural) στάδιος STA/DIOS stádios stad'-ee-os from the base of G2476 (as fixed); a stade or certain measure of distance; by implication, a stadium or race-course:--furlong, race.
entries.4713: στάμνος STA/MNOS stámnos stam'-nos from the base of G2476 (as stationary); a jar or earthen tank:--pot.
entries.4714: στάσις STA/SIS stásis stas'-is from the base of G2476; a standing (properly, the act), i.e. (by analogy) position (existence); by implication, a popular uprising; figuratively, controversy:--dissension, insurrection, X standing, uproar.
entries.4715: στατήρ STATH/R statḗr stat-air' from the base of G2746; a stander (standard of value), i.e. (specially), a stater or certain coin:--piece of money.
entries.4716: σταυρός STAURO/S staurós stow-ros' from the base of G2476; a stake or post (as set upright), i.e. (specially), a pole or cross (as an instrument of capital punishment); figuratively, exposure to death, i.e. self-denial; by implication, the atonement of Christ:--cross.
entries.4717: σταυρόω STAURO/W stauróō stow-ro'-o from G4716; to impale on the cross; figuratively, to extinguish (subdue) passion or selfishness:--crucify.
entries.4718: σταφυλή STAFULH/ staphylḗ staf-oo-lay' probably from the base of G4735; a cluster of grapes (as if intertwined):--grapes.
entries.4719: στάχυς STA/XUS stáchys stakh'-oos from the base of G2476; a head of grain (as standing out from the stalk):--ear (of corn).
entries.4720: Στάχυς *STA/XUS Stáchys stakh'-oos the same as G4719; Stachys, a Christian:--Stachys.
entries.4721: στέγη STE/GH stégē steg'-ay strengthened from a primary τέγος TE/GOS tégos (a "thatch" or "deck" of a building); a roof:--roof.
entries.4722: στέγω STE/GW stégō steg'-o from G4721; to roof over, i.e. (figuratively) to cover with silence (endure patiently):--(for-)bear, suffer.
entries.4723: στείρος STEI/ROS steíros sti'-ros a contraction from G4731 (as stiff and unnatural); "sterile":--barren.
entries.4724: στέλλω STE/LLW stéllō stel'-lo probably strengthened from the base of G2476; properly, to set fast ("stall"), i.e. (figuratively) to repress (reflexively, abstain from associating with):--avoid, withdraw self.
entries.4725: στέμμα STE/MMA stémma stem'-mah from the base of G4735; a wreath for show:--garland.
entries.4726: στεναγμός STENAGMO/S stenagmós sten-ag-mos' from G4727; a sigh:--groaning.
entries.4727: στενάζω STENA/ZW stenázō sten-ad'-zo from G4728; to make (intransitively, be) in straits, i.e. (by implication) to sigh, murmur, pray inaudibly:--with grief, groan, grudge, sigh.
entries.4728: στενός STENO/S stenós sten-os' probably from the base of G2476; narrow (from obstacles standing close about):--strait.
entries.4729: στενοχωρέω STENOXWRE/W stenochōréō sten-okh-o-reh'-o from the same as G4730; to hem in closely, i.e. (figuratively) cramp:--distress, straiten.
entries.4730: στενοχωρία STENOXWRI/A stenochōría sten-okh-o-ree'-ah from a compound of G4728 and G5561; narrowness of room, i.e. (figuratively) calamity:--anguish, distress.
entries.4731: στερεός STEREO/S stereós ster-eh-os' from G2476; stiff, i.e. solid, stable (literally or figuratively):--stedfast, strong, sure.
entries.4732: στερεόω STEREO/W stereóō ster-eh-o'-o from G4731; to solidify, i.e. confirm (literally or figuratively):--establish, receive strength, make strong.
entries.4733: στερέωμα STERE/WMA steréōma ster-eh'-o-mah from G4732; something established, i.e. (abstractly) confirmation (stability):--stedfastness.
entries.4734: Στεφανᾶς *STEFANA=S Stephanâs stef-an-as' probably contraction for στεφανωτός STEFANWTO/S stephanōtós (crowned; from G4737); Stephanas, a Christian:--Stephanas.
entries.4735: στέφανος STE/FANOS stéphanos stef'-an-os from an apparently primary στέφω STE/FW stéphō (to twine or wreathe); a chaplet (as a badge of royalty, a prize in the public games or a symbol of honor generally; but more conspicuous and elaborate than the simple fillet, G1238), literally or figuratively:--crown.
entries.4736: Στέφανος *STE/FANOS Stéphanos stef'-an-os the same as G4735; Stephanus, a Christian:--Stephen.
entries.4737: στεφανόω STEFANO/W stephanóō stef-an-o'-o from G4735; to adorn with an honorary wreath (literally or figuratively):--crown.
entries.4738: στῆθος STH=QOS stēthos stay'-thos from G2476 (as standing prominently); the (entire external) bosom, i.e. chest:--breast.
entries.4739: στήκω STH/KW stḗkō stay'-ko from the perfect tense of G2476; to be stationary, i.e. (figuratively) to persevere:--stand (fast).
entries.4740: στηριγμός STHRIGMO/S stērigmós stay-rig-mos' from G4741; stability (figuratively):--stedfastness.
entries.4741: στηρίζω STHRI/ZW stērízō stay-rid'-zo from a presumed derivative of G2476 (like G4731); to set fast, i.e. (literally) to turn resolutely in a certain direction, or (figuratively) to confirm:--fix, (e-)stablish, stedfastly set, strengthen.
entries.4742: στίγμα STI/GMA stígma stig'-mah from a primary στίζω STI/ZW stízō (to "stick", i.e. prick); a mark incised or punched (for recognition of ownership), i.e. (figuratively) scar of service:--mark.
entries.4743: στιγμή STIGMH/ stigmḗ stig-may' feminine of G4742; a point of time, i.e. an instant:--moment.
entries.4744: στίλβω STI/LBW stílbō stil'-bo apparently a primary verb; to gleam, i.e. flash intensely:--shining.
entries.4745: στοά STOA/ stoá sto-ah' probably from G2476; a colonnade or interior piazza:--porch.
entries.4746: στοιβάς STOIBA/S stoibás stoy-bas' from a primary στείβω STEI/BW steíbō (to "step" or "stamp"); a spread (as if tramped flat) of loose materials for a couch, i.e. (by implication) a bough of a tree so employed:--branch.
